extracted.intended_audience: PR agencies, communications teams and entrants preparing submissions for the Cannes Lions PR (PR Lions) awards
extracted.subtask_description: Rules and judging criteria for submitting PR work to the Cannes Lions PR categories, including weighted judging dimensions and category-specific evaluation guidance across sectors, techniques, social engagement, insights, craft and culture/context.

rubrics_metrics.name: Judging weightings (overall)
rubrics_metrics.description: A number of criteria will be considered during judging, weighted as follows: 20% idea; 30% PR strategy; 20% PR execution; 30% impact and results.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Entrants should structure submissions and evidence to address each weighted area: idea (originality/concept), PR strategy (planning and strategic thinking), PR execution (creative implementation), and impact/results (measured outcomes).

rubrics_metrics.name: Original thinking, transformative insight and earned-media strategy
rubrics_metrics.description: The work should demonstrate how original thinking, transformative insight and a strategy rooted in earned media have influenced opinion and driven progress and change in business, society or culture.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Judges look for evidence that the idea and strategy changed perceptions or created meaningful progress; emphasise earned media approaches and show how insights informed the strategy.

rubrics_metrics.name: Storytelling and reputation/business outcomes
rubrics_metrics.description: The work should have storytelling at its core and establish, protect and enhance the reputation and business of an organisation or brand.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Submissions should show how narrative or storytelling techniques contributed to reputation-building or business objectives; connect creative storytelling to concrete reputation or commercial outcomes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Entry frequency and section repetition rules
rubrics_metrics.description: The same piece of work can be entered up to four times in PR, not including section 'E: Excellence in PR Craft'. However, the same piece of work may only be entered once in ‘A. PR: Sectors’.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Plan category entries accordingly; do not enter the same work more than permitted across sections and respect the single-entry rule for section A.

rubrics_metrics.name: Section E submission eligibility
rubrics_metrics.description: The work in Section E: Excellence in PR Craft can only be submitted and paid for by independent PR agencies or companies owned by a PR network or independent PR network.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Only independent PR agencies or PR network-owned companies may submit to Section E; the same piece can be entered only once in each category within Section E.

rubrics_metrics.name: Subtitles on audiovisual entries
rubrics_metrics.description: Subtitles are highly recommended on all case films, films, demo films and original content.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include subtitles to improve accessibility and clarity for judges viewing audiovisual material.

rubrics_metrics.name: A01 Consumer Goods (sector classification)
rubrics_metrics.description: All fast-moving and durable consumer goods, including but not limited to, food and beverages, toiletries, cleaning products, other household goods, other FMCGs, clothing and accessories, furniture, and consumer electronics.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: * All fast-food entries should be entered into A04. Travel, Leisure, Retail, Restaurants & Fast-Food Chains.

rubrics_metrics.name: A02 Healthcare (sector classification)
rubrics_metrics.description: Pharma, OTC drugs, wellness.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: * If the work has been created for a Charity/NFP then this should be entered into A07.

rubrics_metrics.name: A03 Automotive (sector classification)
rubrics_metrics.description: Vehicles, other automobiles.

rubrics_metrics.name: A04 Travel, Leisure, Retail, Restaurants & Fast-Food Chains (sector classification)
rubrics_metrics.description: All transport- and travel-related services, including public transport and tourism boards. All entertainment- and leisure-related services, including museums, festivals and gyms. All shops, including online shopping, opticians, hairdressers and estate agents. All restaurants and fast food chains, including cafés and bars.

rubrics_metrics.name: A05 Media/Entertainment (sector classification)
rubrics_metrics.description: Music, film, television, publications and media, books, news, digital platforms and other media.

rubrics_metrics.name: A06 Consumer Services/Business to Business (sector classification)
rubrics_metrics.description: All commercial public services, legal, financial, B2B technology, consultancies and professional services, other business services, internal and corporate communications.

rubrics_metrics.name: A07 Not-for-Profit / Charity / Government (sector classification)
rubrics_metrics.description: Government, public information, NGOs, military, charities, non-profit organisations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: * All corporate social responsibility work should be entered in the relevant sector and/or F07. Corporate Purpose & Social Responsibility category in section F.

rubrics_metrics.name: B General: Social Engagement & Influencer Marketing (judging focus)
rubrics_metrics.description: In these categories, your entry will be judged on how well social/digital platforms were leveraged to support or execute the PR campaign.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Make clear how social/digital platforms were used to deliver strategy and outcomes; include platform-specific tactics and results where relevant.

rubrics_metrics.name: B01 Social Engagement
rubrics_metrics.description: Celebrating public relations and social media storytelling that build brand awareness and advocacy. The work should demonstrate how social media was harnessed to increase brand awareness and relevance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Show metrics and examples of how social storytelling drove awareness and advocacy.

rubrics_metrics.name: B02 Community Management
rubrics_metrics.description: Recognising the development, maintenance and nurturing of brand relationships. The work should demonstrate how engaging with a brand's online community/targeted audience built its reputation and established trust and authority within the online community.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide evidence of community-building tactics and their effect on trust, retention or reputation.

rubrics_metrics.name: B03 Real-Time Response
rubrics_metrics.description: Real-time social activity designed to respond to and engage in the conversation around world events, public affairs and other real-world, real-time activity in a creative and meaningful way.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Demonstrate timeliness, relevance, and creative engagement with live events or trending conversations.

rubrics_metrics.name: B04 Content Creation & Production
rubrics_metrics.description: Content created and produced to entertain, inspire or educate. The work should demonstrate how the content created was audience-relevant and engaging as well as in line with brand messaging.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Highlight production quality and audience relevance, and show alignment with brand objectives.

rubrics_metrics.name: B05 Content Discovery & Amplification
rubrics_metrics.description: Recognising a creative approach to content amplification and distribution in order to reach the largest potential audience. The work should demonstrate how a combination of earned, paid, shared and owned media contributed to increased brand engagement and awareness.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explain the amplification mix and attribution of outcomes to different channels (earned/paid/shared/owned).

rubrics_metrics.name: B06 Innovative Use of Influencers/Creators
rubrics_metrics.description: The creative and innovative use of influencers/creators to drive brand message and awareness to a specific audience.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Show originality in influencer use and measurable impact on awareness/engagement with the target audience.

rubrics_metrics.name: C General: Insights & Measurement (judging focus)
rubrics_metrics.description: These categories showcase effectiveness in using data to drive creative inspiration and communications strategies. The work will be judged on the deliberate and thoughtful introduction of insights and measurements to develop campaigns that have had real impact on the performance of an organisation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Demonstrate how insights informed strategy and provide measurement methods and evidence of impact.

rubrics_metrics.name: C01 Research, Data & Analytics
rubrics_metrics.description: Research and data-led or actionable insights that provide a meaningful contribution or input to a public relations programme. The work should provide evidence of research or insight, quality of thinking and the development of a strategy.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include the research methodology, data sources, and how insights fed into strategic decisions.

rubrics_metrics.name: C02 PR Effectiveness
rubrics_metrics.description: Recognises creative work that has a proven impact on business and reputation. The work should provide results data, as well as details of measurement tools and analysis methods used to evaluate results. Consideration will be given to tangible business results and the quality and quantity of media.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide quantitative and qualitative evidence of business/reputation outcomes, and document measurement approaches and tools used.

rubrics_metrics.name: D General: PR Techniques (judging focus)
rubrics_metrics.description: In these categories, your entry will be judged on the creative implementation of your chosen PR technique in order to increase reach and achieve desired campaign outcomes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Focus submissions on the technique used, its creative implementation, and how it delivered reach and outcomes.

rubrics_metrics.name: D01 Media Relations
rubrics_metrics.description: PR that puts journalism at the forefront of the campaign, with evidence of a high degree of innovation intended to engage, educate or influence editorial. The work should explain the relevance of media outcomes, including depth, quality and messaging.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consideration will be given to how this strategy achieved or supported the desired campaign outcome; show editorial impact and message delivery.

rubrics_metrics.name: D02 Use of Events & Stunts
rubrics_metrics.description: Work that uses stunts, events, event sponsorship, competitions, promotional games, street art, guerrilla marketing, launch parties, live shows, live streamed events, festivals, concerts, sporting events, etc. within traditional, digital and new emerging environments to build the value and reputation of a brand or communication project as part of a wider public relations strategy.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explain how the event/stunt was integrated into a wider PR strategy and the outcomes it generated.

rubrics_metrics.name: D03 Launch/Relaunch
rubrics_metrics.description: Work created to launch or relaunch a product or service.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Demonstrate how the launch/relaunch strategy and execution achieved awareness, adoption or other business goals.

rubrics_metrics.name: D04 Brand Voice & Strategic Storytelling
rubrics_metrics.description: Customised strategies designed to communicate a particular point of view/story of a brand/organisation in a consistently relevant way and to build an emotional connection with employees, shareholders and customers alike.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Show consistent voice, narrative strategy and evidence of emotional connection or stakeholder engagement.

rubrics_metrics.name: D05 Use of Technology
rubrics_metrics.description: Existing or new technology that pushes the boundaries of digital innovation to execute or support a PR campaign. This could include, but is not limited to, artificial intelligence, virtual reality, virtual worlds, robotics, gadgets and electronics, wearable and interactive technology, etc. Does not include prototypes of early-stage technology.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Demonstrate how technology was applied to push digital innovation and how it contributed to PR outcomes; exclude early-stage prototypes.

rubrics_metrics.name: D06 Employee Engagement
rubrics_metrics.description: Communications programmes or initiatives designed to inform, educate or inspire employees - engaging internal communities and cultivating strong team dynamics. The work should demonstrate innovative approaches to engaging staff, driving organisational goals and building employee loyalty and satisfaction.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide evidence of measurable employee engagement, satisfaction or business impact from internal communications initiatives.

rubrics_metrics.name: E General: Excellence in PR Craft (judging focus)
rubrics_metrics.description: Work in these categories will be judged on the demonstration of exceptional and creative best practice within the chosen PR specialism.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Entries should showcase outstanding craft and best practice in a PR specialism; note the submission eligibility restrictions for Section E.

rubrics_metrics.name: E01 Corporate Image, Communication & Reputation Management
rubrics_metrics.description: Work that builds the image/raises the profile and shapes the perceptions of a corporate brand, organisation or corporation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Demonstrate strategic approaches to reputation management and evidence of perception/brand profile change.

rubrics_metrics.name: E02 Public Affairs & Lobbying
rubrics_metrics.description: Work planned to influence or inform the public policy agenda using either lobbying or wider public affairs strategies, as well as political or ballot initiatives.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Show planning, tactics, ethical considerations and outcomes related to influencing public policy or public opinion.

rubrics_metrics.name: E03 Crisis Communications & Issue Management
rubrics_metrics.description: The planning and/or handling of the consequences of a crisis or an issue that may affect a company’s credibility and reputation. The work should demonstrate evidence of the planning and/or implementation of a crisis communication strategy and how the desired outcome was achieved.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: * The content of entries in this category can be kept entirely confidential and used for judging purposes only.

rubrics_metrics.name: E04 Internal Communications
rubrics_metrics.description: Engaging internal communications and activities. This may include, but is not limited to, change management, intended to connect employees with a company identity or message. The work should demonstrate how activities translated into measurable results, employee satisfaction and business growth.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Highlight measurable results and connections between internal communications and business/employee outcomes.

rubrics_metrics.name: E05 Sponsorship & Brand Partnership
rubrics_metrics.description: Work that utilised sponsorship and/or partnership programmes in order to meet specific awareness/business goals as well as to enhance the image of a brand, organisation or corporation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Demonstrate how sponsorships/partnerships were structured to deliver awareness and business/brand benefits.

rubrics_metrics.name: F General: Culture & Context (judging focus)
rubrics_metrics.description: Work that is brought to life through cultural insights and regional context.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explain how cultural or regional context informed strategy, creativity and outcomes; show relevance to the target audience.

rubrics_metrics.name: F01 Local Brand
rubrics_metrics.description: Work for brands distributed solely within a specific locality. The work should resonate with a clearly defined, local target audience.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Demonstrate local relevance and resonance with a defined local audience.

rubrics_metrics.name: F02 Challenger Brand
rubrics_metrics.description: Brands that have creatively adapted their approach in response to competitor pressure by challenging the status quo to create game-changing work that uses progressive thinking and innovative creativity.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Show how the brand challenged category norms and created distinctive impact versus competitors.

rubrics_metrics.name: F03 Single-Market Campaign
rubrics_metrics.description: Work that aired or ran in a single country / region / market. The work should describe how the campaign was designed for the specific target market.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explain market-specific strategy, cultural adaptation and outcomes in that market.

rubrics_metrics.name: F04 Social Behaviour
rubrics_metrics.description: Work inspired by a specific audience or community, relying on identifiable social behaviour. The work should demonstrate how leveraging insights into consumer behaviour can create a powerful connection with a brand.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide behavioural insight sources and show how those insights translated into campaign design and results.

rubrics_metrics.name: F05 Use of Humour
rubrics_metrics.description: Work that celebrates the art of humour in branded communications. Infusing wit, satire, and cleverness into campaigns that provide amusement and create memorable, laughter-inducing connections with audiences.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Demonstrate the role of humour in craft and outcomes, and evidence of audience reception.

rubrics_metrics.name: F06 Breakthrough on a Budget
rubrics_metrics.description: Creative use of modest budgets and/or resources in relation to the market and/or industry to create maximum impact. The work should demonstrate how fresh insight, smart spending and compelling strategic thinking solved a business problem despite limited resources.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Show budget context and explain how strategic choices maximised impact relative to resources.

rubrics_metrics.name: F07 Corporate Purpose & Social Responsibility
rubrics_metrics.description: Purpose-driven work/brand activism that addresses social, ethical and environmental issues. The work should demonstrate how the brand’s purpose has created value and affected communities by connecting customers to culture.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: * All not-for-profit, charity or government work should be entered in the relevant sector and/or A07. Not-for-profit / Charity / Government category in section A. PR: Sectors.

rubrics_metrics.name: F08 Market Disruption
rubrics_metrics.description: Brands that have creatively adapted their strategy in response to local / regional / global issues, embracing new ways of delivering their brand while showing consideration for the consumer.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Describe strategic adaptations and how they delivered differentiation and consumer consideration.

rubrics_metrics.name: F09 Cultural Engagement
rubrics_metrics.description: Work crafted around strategic solutions rooted in the lived experiences of culturally grounded communities. Work which reflects and translates the nuances of customs, behaviours, and traditions that shape foundational perspectives on identity (e.g. disability, gender, race, orientation, age). Such insights reveal how audiences choose brands and media experiences, driving growth and impact.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Show culturally grounded insights, sensitivity, and the ways these informed creative strategy and measurable impact.
